prompt: You're pairing with a distributed file-storage team on their CDN backend. Uploaded files are split into fixed-size chunks and content-addressed by SHA-256 so identical chunks dedup automatically and can be integrity-checked later. A senior engineer reports two related symptoms in production: dedup mysteriously never hits on some files, and periodic integrity sweeps flag certain chunks as "corrupt" even though reading them back byte-for-byte looks perfectly fine. Below is the chunker's split-and-hash loop — walk through it and find exactly why this happens.
